failure_summary.description: Follow-ups reran hotel searches or used proximity instead of filtering the relevant cached results.
Several trajectories failed to save tool results or referenced undefined result variables.
Earlier cuisine preferences were lost or criteria and locations were mapped incorrectly or invented.
Round trips were represented as one outbound search with an arrival date rather than two directional searches.
A hotel search missing required stay dates did not prompt for them while proceeding with the complete restaurant request.

patch.reasoning: Most observed errors are already covered by explicit cache, tool-persistence, field-mapping, flight-leg, and required-input rules, so repeating those rules would not patch a gap. The remaining gap is making clear that active user constraints must carry forward when a request becomes searchable on a later turn, including when no cached result exists.

edits.target: Accepting an offer to search a new domain, category, or entity creates that search using established trip context.
edits.content: Maintain active supported constraints for each domain across the full conversation. When making a new search, include all still-active criteria the user has already supplied, even if the latest turn only supplies a location or another missing detail. When filtering, account for active criteria not already embodied in the cached result as well as newly supplied criteria. Drop or replace a constraint only when the user withdraws or changes it.
